description: The bar chart illustrates the correlation values across two domains—“Movies” and “Songs”—for four distinct measures: PopGT, PopGe, RPopGT, and RPopGe, as referenced in the paper “How Knowledge Popularity Influences and Enhances LLM Knowledge Boundary Perception.” The vertical y-axis, labeled “Correlation,” ranges from 0 to 0.7 in increments of 0.1, representing the strength of correlation. The horizontal x-axis categorizes the data into “Movies” and “Songs,” with each category containing four grouped bars corresponding to the four measures, differentiated by color and pattern: PopGT (solid orange), PopGe (orange with diagonal stripes), RPopGT (solid blue), and RPopGe (blue with diagonal stripes). In the “Movies” group, RPopGe shows the highest correlation (~0.63), followed by RPopGT (~0.35), PopGT (~0.22), and PopGe (~0.10). In the “Songs” group, RPopGe again exhibits the highest correlation (~0.70), followed by RPopGT (~0.50), PopGT (~0.30), and PopGe (~0.09). A gray bar appears beneath the “Songs” label but is unlabeled and unexplained in the legend, suggesting it may be a placeholder or an artifact. Overall, the chart visually emphasizes that RPopGe consistently achieves the highest correlation in both domains, while PopGe consistently shows the lowest.
